title: What If Earth Had the Gravity of Mars?

scenes.text: What if Earth had the gravity of Mars? You'd feel light, and your bones would pay for it.
Mars has about one third of Earth's gravity, so you would weigh roughly a third of what you do now.
Your bones are built by carrying weight. Without that load, astronauts lose about 1 to 1.5 percent of bone density per month.
In one study of 17 astronauts, nine had not fully recovered after a year back on Earth.
Missions to Mars are modelled to leave about a third of astronauts at risk of osteoporosis after three years.
So a lighter world feels like a gift, but gravity is the gym your skeleton never leaves.
